sentences.text: 1. The present appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 at the instance of the appellants- original claimants being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 09.09.2021 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Vadodara in MACP No.867 of 2013.

By the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has though partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the present appellants- original NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/09/2025 undefined claimants under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1966") holding them entitled to Atul Surendra Chitre vs Heirs Of Undaybhai Madhukar Raje ... on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181048181/
1 recover an amount of Rs.4,60,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% pa from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs, from the original opponents - respondents herein, jointly and severally, however has not entertained their claim for compensation of entire amount of Rs.32 lakhs.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, present appeal seeking enhancement of the amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.3,50,000/- additionally.

2. This Court at the stage of admission hearing of the appeal, upon considering the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellants noticing the fact that the deceased was homemaker and was also running tuition class and earning income by working as insurance agent, by order dated 1.7.2022 had admitted the appeal to reconsider the issue of quantum of compensation vis-a-vis income of the deceased.
3. Notice of admission of appeal has been duly served upon the respondent nos. 1 and 2.

No appearance has been entered NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
03/09/2025 undefined on behalf of respondent no.1 being owner of the vehicle involved.
Respondent no.2 is represented by the learned advocate Mr. V.C.Thomas.
The matter was taken up for final hearing with the assistance of the learned advocate on record for the respective parties.
4. Learned advocate for the appellant at the outset has submitted that the present appeal is confined to the limited issue of income of the deceased being determined on lower side.

Learned advocate has invited my attention to the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and has submitted that though the Tribunal has considered the income tax returns for the AY 2008-09 produced on record at Exh.38 wherein the income of the deceased as reflected as Rs.7805/- per month derived from her vocation and additionally rendering her services as a housewife, the Tribunal has confined to determine the notional monthly income of deceased as Rs.3000/- only.
The attention of this Court was invited to the foundational facts of the case, which in absence of any appeal being filed by the respondent has remained uncontroverted.

According to learned advocate, no sound reasons has been assigned by the Tribunal while discarding NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/09/2025 undefined the case of the claimants about the income of the deceased of Rs.7805/- per annum, which is established by leading evidence in the nature of income tax return.

The learned advocate had pointed out that considering the fact that accident had occurred in 2013 and the consumer price index and the cost of inflation index in 2013, the monthly income of the deceased ought to have been considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.

In order to substantiate his claim, learned advocate had placed reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Arun Kumar Agrawal and another versus National Insurance Company Ltd and others reported in (2010) 9 SCC 218, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognised the gratuitous service rendered by the wife or the mother to her family, which cannot be equated with the services of an employee and where no evidence or data is possible to estimate the value of such services.

entities.text: Arun Kumar Agrawal and another versus National Insurance Company Ltd and others reported in (2010) 9 SCC 218
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However,
the Court has fixed the notional income of the non-earning person by referring to the yardstick of clause (6) of second schedule.
The Court has also criticized the approach of the High Court to compute the compensation in such cases by equating it with the case of skilled worker and minimum wages payable.

Learned advocate has also NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/09/2025 undefined assailed the impugned judgement on the ground that the Tribunal failed to appreciate the landmark judgments of the Honourable Supreme Court in the Atul Surendra Chitre vs Heirs Of Undaybhai Madhukar Raje ... on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181048181/
2 case of New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Somwati and Ors reported in (2020) 9 SCC 644 and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhur Ram & Ors reported in (2018)18 SCC 130, while considering the amount of consortium which otherwise each of the claimants are entitled to.

sentences.text: Learned advocate has therefore urged the Court to allow the present appeal and to enhance the amount of compensation appropriately.

5. Per contra, learned advocate Mr. V C Thomas appearing for respondent no.2 Insurance Company has objected to the aforesaid submissions made by learned advocate for the appellants original claimants.

Learned advocate for the respondent no.2 has mainly relied upon the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and has submitted that in absence of any corroborative documentary evidence being brought on record to substantiate their claim with regard to independent income being earned by the deceased by running tuition class and working as insurance agent, the Tribunal has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
03/09/2025 undefined considering her services rendered as a housewife, notionally fixed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.3000/- at the time of accident.

As regards the submission made by learned advocate with regard to dependency loss is concerned, learned advocate had fairly pointed out that the Tribunal has followed the settled principles of law as laid down in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi & ors reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 by extending 25% rise towards future prospects on the aforesaid income and has accordingly considered annual income with future prospects to the tune of Rs.45,000/- per annum (Rs.36,000/-
+ Rs.9000/-).

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi & ors reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Noticing number of dependents in the family, the Tribunal has applied 1/3rd deduction and has accordingly considered net annual income of Rs.30,000/- per annum and by applying multiplier of 13, has determined loss of dependency to the extent of Rs.3,90,000/-.
In addition to the aforeasid amount, Tribunal has also considered the awarding Rs.15,000/- each under the respective heads of funeral expenses and loss of estate.

As regards the amount of compensation under the head of loss of consortium is concerned, learned advocate could not dispute the judgements relied upon by learned advocate for the original NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/09/2025 undefined appellants and has urged this Court to pass appropriate order noticing the fact that the legal representatives of the deceased include the husband of the deceased and their two childrens.

6. Considering the aforesaid submissions of learned advocates appearing for the respective parties in light of the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal, the only question which arises for consideration of this Court is as to whether the Tribunal committed any error in determining the amount of compensation in a claim petition preferred by the present appellant under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, by holding the present respondents- original opponents jointly and severely liable to pay the amount of compensation as Rs.4,60,000/- with interest and cost ?
7. I have carefully considered the submissions of learned advocate on record for the original claimants in light of the record and proceedings being placed for consideration with the present appeal.

On careful consideration of the pleadings made by the original claimants in the claim petition and the evidence of the husband of the deceased who has entered the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/09/2025 undefined witness box and has deposed before the Tribunal at Exh.21.

In his examination in chief affidavit, the said witness has categorically stated Atul Surendra Chitre vs Heirs Of Undaybhai Madhukar Raje ... on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181048181/
3 that the deceased was a homemaker and was rendering her service towards the household activities.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the same time, the deceased used to earn independent income of Rs.10,000/- pa by doing work of insurance agent.
She also used to conduct private tuition classes at home through which she used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month.
Because of her untimely death due to motor vehicle accident, the family of the deceased have certainly lost the financial help.

Upon appreciation of cross examination of the deceased, the only fact which is brought on record by the respondent no.2 - insurance company is that no documentary proof of her income has been brought on record.
No other evidence rebutting the aforesaid claim of the original claimants has been brought on record by respondent No.2 -Insurance Company.
In absence of any contradictory evidence being brought on record, this court is required to examine the income of the deceased in light of the evidence brought on record.

Though the original claimants, in cross examination has admitted that no proof of the income of the deceased has been produced on record, however, bare perusal of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/09/2025 undefined document produced at Exhibit 38, the income tax returns of the deceased are very much on record.

The accident had occurred on 7th May 2010 and the ITR returns of assessment year 2008-09 is submitted on 20 th July 2009 and verified on 31st July 2008 has been produced on record wherein the gross total income of the deceased for AY 2008-09 is reflected as Rs.7805/- p.a from her business.
It is an undisputed fact that the deceased was a housewife and was attending household chores thereby rendering her services to the family.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court on various occasioned have recognized the contribution made by the wife / mother to the house, being invaluable, which cannot be computed in terms of money.

Noticing the gratuitous services rendered by them, with true love and affection to the children as well as to her husband and managing the household affairs round the clock with her constant attendance, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Arun Kumar Agrawal (supra) as relied upon by learned advocate for the appellants- original claimants has found the order of the Tribunal and the High Court erroneous and unjustified evaluating the service of the deceased housewife at Rs.1250/- per month and has enhanced the award from Rs.2,50,000/- to Rs.6,00,000/-.

From the analysis NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
03/09/2025 undefined of the findings of the Tribunal as recorded in the said decision, it transpires that the Tribunal had noted that at the time of accident, in view of clause (6) of second schedule of the Act of 1988, the income of deceased was assessed at Rs.5,000/- per month (Rs.60,000/- per annum), and after making deduction of Rs.20,000/- towards personal expenses of the deceased and applying multiplier of 15, the loss of dependency was assessed as Rs. 6,00,000/-.

However, at the final stage of pronouncement of the award, the Tribunal had reduced Rs.2,50,000/- by observing that the deceased was actually not an earning member and since the assessment is solely based on notional income, the amount of compensation was found to be much higher and thereby reduced the aforesaid amount from the total amount of compensation.

In the appeal before the High Court,
the Court took the view that the claimant include the husband of the deceased and their child aged 7 years.

The Court observed that neither of the claimants were dependent upon the deceased and therefore, estimating the service rendered by the deceased as housewife at Rs. 1,250/- per month and her annual contribution towards such services being quantified to Rs.15,000/- by applying multiplier of 15, had awarded loss of dependency to the extent NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/09/2025 undefined of Rs. 2,25,000/-.

Further, by adding amount of Rs. 3,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.7,000/- towards loss of love and affection and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of comfort and consortium, the High Court awarded total amount of Atul Surendra Chitre vs Heirs Of Undaybhai Madhukar Raje ... on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181048181/
4 compensation to Rs.2,50,000/-.

sentences.text: As against the aforesaid orders passed by the Tribunal on the High Court, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the appeal, set aside the aforesaid orders and held the appellant's original claimants entitled to total amount of compensation of Rs.6 lakhs.
That applying the aforesaid principles in the facts of the present case, the annual income of the deceased is reconsidered and assessed as Rs. 5,500/- per month.

Considering her age of 46 years at the time of accident, in light of the decision of Constitutional Bench in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), an amount of 25% future rise of the aforesaid income is required to be considered towards future prospects i.e. Rs.5500/- + 25% rise = Rs.6875/-.

Considering the 1/3rd deduction for personal expenses viz. Rs.2292/- the net annual income of the deceased is considered as Rs. 4583/-
multiplied by 12.Thus, loss of dependency, by applying multiplier of 13, is determined as Rs.
7,14,948/-.

As regards the submission made by learned Advocate for the appellants -original claimants with regard to NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/09/2025 undefined loss of consortium is concerned, considering the fact that the family of the deceased consisted of her husband and two major children
, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company (supra) is inclined to accept enhancement of the aforesaid amount.

In view of the aforesaid principles laid down, noticing the fact that the Tribunal pronounced impugned judgment in 2021, ought to have awarded each of the original claimants/ appellants herein an amount of Rs.44,800/- towards loss of consortium by giving 10%
rise to the amount of consortium as fixed in case of Pranay Sethi(Supra) in 2017.
Thus, the total amount of compensation under the head of loss of consortium is revised and enhanced to Rs.1,45,200/-.

As regards the amount of compensation awarded under the other conventional heads are concerned, the same is required to be reconsidered and enhanced to Rs.18,150/- under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses respectively.

8. For the foregoing reasons, the total amount of compensation under different heads is reconsidered and enhanced as under:

Future loss of income 7,14,948/-
 Loss of Consortium 1,45,200  Loss of Estate 18,150/-
 Loss of funeral expenses 18,150/-
Total Compensation 8,96,448  Awarded by the Tribunal 4,60,000  Enhanced amount 4,36,448 9.
For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is allowed.

The interim judgment and award dated 09.09.2021 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Vadodara in MACP No.867 of 2013 is hereby modified to the extent by holding the original claimants /appellants herein entitled to recover total amount of compensation of Rs.8,96,448/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate cost, to be realised from Atul Surendra Chitre vs Heirs Of Undaybhai Madhukar Raje ...

The respondent No. 2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit enhanced amount of compensation of Rs.4,36,448/- (Rs.8,96,448/-minus Rs.4,60,000/-), with proportionate cost and interest to be deposited within period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

On deposit of the aforesaid NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/197/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/09/2025 undefined amount of compensation, the Tribunal shall be at liberty to proceed with the apportionment, release and disbursement of the entire award amount in favour of the appellants- original claimants subject to due verification and strictly in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in this regard.
Let the aforesaid exercise be undertaken by the Tribunal within period of 2 weeks from deposit of the entire award amount.
With these observations the first appeal stands disposed of.
The Record and Proceedings are directed to be remitted back to the concerned Tribunal along with the writ.
